g.text: MarieRank1Convo1 begins.
Bonjour, bonjour, Drifter ! How are you this fine day ? Or evening. I truly do not know what time it is in this place.
I am certain one of these bibelots that Monsieur Loid keeps is a clock, but I cannot for the life of me determine which it is.
I fear to touch any device in this strange sanctum. I fully believe I am just as liable to send myself careening into some far-flung distant time as I am to warm a cup of tea.
It's probably best not to press any buttons you aren't certain about, no.
I'm sure you'll be fine.
[End.]
Very good advice, indeed. I have heard from Monsieur Loid that you had your own aventure temporelle. I wonder -
C'est très gentil de votre part, but... you are not the one who has been thrown into another... ah. Right. Yes !
Chat ends.
Was it as dangerous as this one ?
You would know, wouldn't you. Forgive me. Was your own personal adventure as dangerous as this one ?
The time period? Or my stay there in particular?
It was different, but I promise you're safe here.
+10 Chemistry
I very much appreciate your rousing vote of confidence, but I do not precisely share it. Especially not when I have such trouble simply discerning the time.
Good to make the distinction. I hardly doubt your experience with the past was "normal" by aggregate standards. I certainly hope not, by the tell of it.
One would expect there to be one in the corner of this... "screen" here, but there is not ! Mauvaise qualité, if you ask me.
I meant the "time period" itself. Allow me to rephrase -
Regardless, we have wandered quite far from my question !
Was this "past" era that you traveled to, that is indeed far closer to the "farther past" from which I hail, more or less latently dangerous than this time in which we currently find ourselves ?
(Goodness ! I do love this, I must say it is far more interesting than dusting communionware.)
I think it's about the same. The weaponry is different and they might not know what they're up against yet, but war is war and death is death.
I think this time is less dangerous. We have more ability to deal with the challenges we're facing. They're just getting started.
I think this time is more dangerous. While we still have the Infested in common, they were dealing with far more rudimentary weaponry.
Honestly, I'm just glad you're enjoying yourself. It can be a lot to adapt to all at once.
+5 Chemistry
You may be right. I will think on it. Thank you.
+5 Chemistry
Like all things, I suppose it would be relative, non ? The predator that kills us now is just as deadly as that which hunted us then. It just sharpens its teeth.
Chat ends.
I was prepared for this by le Cardinal Dimanche - your Albrecht Entrati. Unlike my dear Lyon, I believed his words as fact. And unlike Lyon, I see this as our great adventure, not a burden.
Unless you're Orokin, who found a way to avoid death... in theory, if not in practice.
I'm also happy that you're adapting well to the future.
Service to the Luminaries needn't be an act of suffering. In this, we have always differed.
And I believe the devil is a perfect example of why death is the greatest gift that Lua has ever given us.
+5 Chemistry
Update boolean MarieLyonSuffering1
Update boolean MarieRoathe1
I was prepared for this by le Cardinal Dimanche - your Albrecht Entrati. Unlike my dear Lyon, I believed his words as fact. And unlike Lyon, I see this as our great adventure, not a burden.
And do not avoid my question, silly ! Which do you think is more dangerous ?

Oh ! Now that is the sound of a clock I do recognize, though I still cannot identify where the blasted thing is located. Either way, I fear I must go. This has been delightful. Until we can "meet" again ! Aux Dieux !
Service to the Luminaries needn't be an act of suffering. In this, we have always differed.
I believe this time is more deadly. We have how many impossible enemies trying to kill us?
I believe our time is less dangerous. They are just discovering new ways of killing each other. Our ways are just a bit more exciting in looks, perhaps.
I believe it is probably about equal, in the end. Death is death, isn't it?
Chat ends.
Update boolean MarieLyonSuffering1
You may be right. I will think on it. Thank you.
+5 Chemistry
Chat ends.
Like all things, I suppose it would be relative, no ? The predator that kills us now is just as deadly as that which hunted us then. It just sharpens its teeth.
As someone who tries to defend against the wolf, I often find myself exhausted by this.
Unless you're Orokin, who found a way to avoid death... in theory, if not in practice.
I think you, my dear Drifter, are more likely to run off to join the pack of wolves than to sit guard against it. And I do mean that as a compliment.
And I believe the devil is a perfect example of why death is the greatest gift that Lua has ever given us.
Update boolean MarieRoathe1
